newsitem.title: USA: Insured munis hit record 49 pct in 96 - Reuter poll.
newsitem.headline: Insured munis hit record 49 pct in 96 - Reuter poll.

text.p: Municipal bond insurance companies backed a record 49 percent of the market in 1996, insuring $87.4 billion of the $180 billion of new issues sold during the year, according a Reuter poll of the industry.
MBIA Insurance Corp, a unit of MBIA Inc, was again the market share leader for the year, with $34.1 billion or 39 percent of the market.

Neil Budnick, director of MBIA's public finance operation, said the overall industry's nearly 50 percent penetration rate is sustainable in 1997. "There was a time when people said you can never pass 20, 30 and now 50 percent," Budnick said in a recent interview.
AMBAC Indemnity Corp, a unit of AMBAC Inc, was the second most-active muni insurer last year, applying its AAA rating to $25 billion, or 29 percent of the market.
Joseph Salzano, executive vice president at AMBAC, agreed that the 50 percent penetration level would continue this year.
He predicted overall volume for the year would rise about five to seven percent.

Financial Guaranty Insurance Co, a unit of GE Capital Services, maintained its third place market share ranking despite deciding not to insure certain sectors of the market that it considers too unpredictable for a 30-year insurance guarantee.
"We have a narrower scope than some of our competitors and that's because our view of the risk is different from some of our competitors," said Vernon Endo, managing director at FGIC.
FGIC said it insured $16 billion of muni bonds for the year, or 18.3 percent of the market, down from 21 percent in 1995.
GE Capital is a unit of General Electric Co.
Rounding out the top four players in the market was Financial Security Assurance, a unit of Financial Security Assurance Holdings Ltd.

FSA said it insured $11.2 billion of bonds for the year. That compares to a total of $6.7 billion FSA and Capital Guaranty Insurance Co insured in 1995. FSA acquired Capital Guaranty in December 1995. FSA's market share jumped to almost 13 percent in 1996 from almost 10 percent for the combined companies the year before.

"We were very happy with the volume we were able to write," Roger Taylor, chief operating officer at FSA, said in an interview. Taylor said the company made significant progress in 1996 in its goal of eliminating the spread between FSA-insured bonds and yields on bonds insured by the company's larger competitors. He said the spread disappeared entirely in several areas.
